pr_title: Fix missing host variables on stream
pr_body:
##### Summary
Fixes #9375 

We were not copying properly the data between buffer and with this the HOST variables were not properly copied to the parent.
##### Component Name
Stream
##### Test Plan
1 - Compile this PR mainly on children hosts.
2 - Start parent and after few seconds start the slave.
3 - Do the following request for the parent `https://localhost:19999/host/CHILD_NAME/api/v1/alarm_variables?chart=system.load` and check if the variable `active_processors` is present.
4 - Repeat the steps 1, 2 and 3 at least three times.

##### Additional Information
pr_comments:
Manage this branch in Squash

Test this branch here: https://thiagoftsmfix-receiver-hpx2g.squash.io

issue_context.title: Some agents not setting $active_processors alarm variable
issue_context.body:
<!---
When asking a new question please:
- Verify first that your question wasn't asked before on GitHub. 
  HINT: Use label "question" when searching for such issues.
- Briefly explain what is the problem you are having
- Try to provide as much information about your environment (OS distribution,
  running in container, etc.) as possible to allow us reproduce this bug faster.
- Write which component is affected. We group our components the same way our
  code is structured so basically:
    component name = dir in top level directory of repository
- Provide a clear and concise description of what you expected to happen.
-->

##### Question summary
I am running a distributed setup with ~10 hosts streaming to a central server. Lately, I have been receiving a lot of "high system load" alerts. After some checking, I found that the `$active_processors` alarm variable is not being set on most of my systems, so the alarm is defaulting to 2 cpu cores (when most of my systems are 8+). When checking `https://my.central.server/host/specific.node/api/v1/alarm_variables?chart=system.load`, there is no `active_processors` variable under `host_variables` on the systems affected.

What's the best why I can debug this? I checked docs and I did not find a way to debug _internal_ plugins, like `proc.plugin`.
Thanks!

##### OS / Environment
Central host: Ubuntu 18
Most streaming nodes: Ubuntu 18

##### Component Name
`system.load`

##### Expected results
comments: also posted on reddit about the issue: https://www.reddit.com/r/netdata/comments/h9jj11/excessive_system_load_alerts_active_processors/

Hi @willhseitz,

Please, can you run the shell script `./daemon/system-info.sh` that is inside netdata repo on a system that is not setting properly the variable and give us the output?

best regards!
@thiagoftsm thanks, is there an email I can send the info to, please?

Hi @willhseitz ,

Thank you very much to report us the problem and to send me the email, thanks your email I could eliminate a possible source of problem.
I tested Netdata 1.22.1  as child and I observed that the missed variable was present with it, I also tested the latest version of Netdata and I could not find more the variable.
Please, can you run the command `netdata -v` on a host that has the variable present? I am working with the team now to find the PR that removed this variable.

Best regards!

All my servers are set to autoupdate on the nightly build. Both with and without variable are on `netdata v1.22.1-303-nightly`.

In case it helps, I just emailed the system-info for one of our servers that _does_ have the variable set

Hi @willhseitz ,

Today I discovered that we are having problems on sender process that is not sending sometimes the missing variables to the receiver process.
We will work to fix this during this week.

best regards!

Hi @thiagoftsm and @amoss , I manually updated some systems that didnt have the host variables via the kickstart script to `v1.22.1-318-nightly`, but I am still not getting those variables some times. Is #9396 included in the nightly build?

Hi @willhseitz ,

It looks like that our kickstart has a problem, I am running the latest Netdata now, and we have the version `netdata v1.22.1-331-g641a4592` not the version you are running.
@Ferroin, please, can you confirm the version of the latest nightly?

Best regards!

Hello @willhseitz ,

I retest now using a VM and I observed that the variable was sent to `receiver`. I decided to expand the test to be sure that this was not a coincidence, so I created 10 LXC clients and I configured the stream on them. When they connected to the `receiver` all hosts sent the correct variables, please, can you also update the `receiver` to confirm that the problem was fixed? I am believing that thanks the fact the master was not updated or restarted, the problem persists.

Best regards!

I don't think that the version running on the parent node (receiver) will make a difference. As long as the child node (sender) is running the new code the problem should be fixed. Can we find out why the kickstart has delivered the old version (@prologic / @Ferroin ) ?

@willhseitz hi

the fix was not in the nightly at that moment, now it is, you need to update your nd instances one more time

@willhseitz, it turns out that working out which commits were in the nightly was slightly more complex that we realized. @ilyam8 has a nice trick for doing it:
```
git rev-list $(git describe --abbrev=0)..HEAD --reverse | awk NR==318
```
This shows that the nightly was the day before the fix was merged. The nightly that had index `337` and onwards contain the fix.

> I don't think that the version running on the parent node (receiver) will make a difference. As long as the child node (sender) is running the new code the problem should be fixed. Can we find out why the kickstart has delivered the old version (@prologic / @Ferroin ) ?

I am thinking that this can be another bug, all the tests that I made with success had a common pattern, I compiled both parent and children. It is possible that when the child is sending the data, some variables are not updated.

review_comments: Acquiring and releasing the lock twice (and also duplicating the copy from the build into the circular buffer) is less efficient. Was there a reason not to move the call into the locked section?
Yes,  I moved it there and the problem persists.
Are the callbacks deferred or do they happen during the call?
